rv.q: El Guindi's play is sharp and engaging, and contains promise. The sheer heft and timeliness of the material makes for an intriguing evening of theater.
People of the Book is, without a doubt, a true masterpiece.
El Guindi couldn't seem to decide which of these conflicts is the crux of the story, and they are melded together awkwardly and dramatized in ways that don't make sense.
